LATEST UPDATE
September 20, 2026
UPDATES - SEPTEMBER 20, 2026
Upgraded the Risk Fight opponent to v4, with improved combo timing and finishing pressure.
Fixed bolt and blood-spell projectiles appearing too early and stopping short of their target.
Starting PID is now a fresh 50/50 roll each fight. Click the PID indicator to give it to the other player.
NH stake and DMM keep the same models and decision logic as the previous live release.
UPDATES - SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
Released Risk Fight: practise Webweaver bow, granite maul, Elder maul, and Vengeance combos against its own trained opponent.
Risk Fight arrows now have visible projectiles and distance-based hit timing, with off-PID hits landing one tick later.
Added exact opponent hitpoints, including zero HP, to the default opponent panel.
Clicking All hides the chatbox and reveals the world underneath without zooming or recentering the camera.
Walking, eating, drinking, or equipping gear cancels granite-maul auto-targeting. Preloaded specs still release when you click the opponent.
Fixed Risk Fight Vengeance level checks, food and incoming-hit ordering, and lethal melee PID ordering.
Recoil rings now deplete correctly; the default Risk Fight kit includes a spare ring in place of one summer pie.
Corrected equipment-slot placeholders, weapon-style icons, and the auto-retaliate label across all three modes.
Improved initial prayer-tab loading, spell-reordering feedback, and Risk Fight's Lunar spellbook icons.
UPDATES - SEPTEMBER 17, 2026
Fixed missing XP drops from instant melee hits, including Armadyl godsword attacks and specials.
Added independent four- or five-tick attack speed settings for Zuriel's staff and crossbows in DMM.
DMM now uses the improved ornate granite maul visuals and special-attack preloading behavior.
Added an eye button to hide the practice controls; hover over the dimmed eye to reveal them.
PID stays visible when the controls are hidden and sits above the special-attack buttons by default.
Attack now replaces a queued manual spell while preserving configured autocast.
Eating can free inventory space for a two-handed weapon switch in the same tick.
Removing two equipment items in one tick preserves both changes.
Using an inventory item no longer also eats or equips the target on mouse release.
Blood-spell healing uses the equipment worn when casting, including Zuriel's staff's healing bonus.
Added Remove trees / Restore trees, with cleared tiles available for movement and an updated minimap.
UPDATES - AUGUST 5, 2026
DMM opponent upgraded to teacher165, the v26 ranged multi-gear prayer checkpoint: the best prayer reading of the top Elo league finishers, a balanced magic/ranged/melee mix, and strong expected damage per fight.
Added the Elo league: every compatible checkpoint and scripted opponent played one full fight against every other entrant (313 entrants, 48,828 fights). teacher165 was picked as the deployed model because it was the most balanced of the top three - the leader was a no-opponent-prayer ablation and second place had noticeably weaker prayer reading.
Deployed model parity is now gate-checked against the Java checkpoint: defence-prayer and policy-boundary replay gates pass within 1e-5 score tolerance.
Fixed the resizable-mode minimap mask so it uses the real source mask sprite and scales with the client frame instead of assuming a fixed 145x151 mask.
Fixed same-tick combat resolution order (PID): an attack now resolves against the defender's pre-movement tile when the defender already moved earlier in the same tick, matching Java's player-processing order.
Removed the old aim trainer section; the site is now the NH practice client with NH stake and DMM setups.
UPDATES - JUNE 15, 2026
Hard mode now uses neural models for both NH stake and DMM setups.
DMM Hard is using the direct-gear Java DMM checkpoint with explicit action IDs matched to the Java/TypeScript action bridge.
Both large neural hard-mode models now load through deployable chunks.
PID and vengeance trinket overlays are Alt-draggable and no longer overlap by default; fight deaths reset back to setup selection.
UPDATES - JUNE 10, 2026
Public opponents were simplified to one Hard option, with the selected setup choosing the model.
NH stake Hard uses the expanded continuation model: 11,604,230 parameters, three 256-unit hidden layers, and 44,550 action outputs.
The large NH stake model is served through deployable chunks so the hosted build can load it reliably.
UPDATES - JUNE 6, 2026
Camera zoom, fixed-client framing, context-menu anchoring, and menu close timing were tightened against source behavior.
VLS regular attacks, spell/combat sounds, and sequence playback received parity fixes.
Main-client mouse-wheel zoom now stays inside the client instead of scrolling the page.
UPDATES - JUNE 5, 2026
DMM setup added with the captured inventory, new gear, and its own hard-mode policy path.
Noxious halberd, Voidwaker, VLS, Zaryte crossbow, trinket of vengeance, and bolt procs are wired in.
Game sounds, continuous audio sliders, camera zoom, right-click timing, and combat animation parity were tightened.
UPDATES - JUNE 4, 2026
Hard-mode policy evaluation gained runtime head-to-head and cohort checks.
The public shell was simplified around the playable trainer instead of internal workbench controls.
UPDATES - JUNE 1, 2026
Hard policy and camera framing were refreshed.
Overlay projection and camera-wheel checks were expanded to catch fixed-client framing regressions.

Free OSRS NH and tribrid PvP practice

NH Trainer is a free, open-source browser practice client for Old School RuneScape-style PvP. Fight a trained AI opponent using NH stake or DMM setups, and practise gear switches, protection prayers, movement and supply timing without risking items or using a player account.

How to start practising
Choose NH stake or DMM in the trainer above. Each setup loads its own Hard AI opponent.
Arrange your inventory and equipment before the fight. Use Save setup to keep your setup in this browser.
Wait for the opponent to load, then press Start. Focus on one skill at a time: clean switches, prayer changes or staying in control of your supplies.
What are NH and tribrid fights?

NH means “no honour”, a style of OSRS PvP that uses protection prayers and switches between melee, ranged and magic. Tribrid practice brings those three attack styles together: changing your gear, choosing an attack and defending against the opponent's next move.

Use repeated fights to work on switching accurately under pressure, responding with the right prayer, moving around freezes and finding time to eat or restore prayer.

Practise against a trained AI opponent

The opponent learns through self-play and chooses gear, prayers, attacks, movement and supplies from the fight state. The public trainer offers Hard difficulty, with the selected NH stake or DMM setup deciding which opponent model is loaded.

Read the NH AI training blog for the development story and how the opponents were trained.

Do I need to download a client or log in?

No download or RuneScape login is needed. The trainer runs in a browser with JavaScript and WebGL enabled. Your settings and saved setup stay in this browser. A mouse and keyboard give you the intended practice controls.

This is a standalone practice simulation. It does not connect to the live game, use player accounts or transfer items or progress into OSRS.
